questions.explain: A learned model understands context — e.g., that 72% CPU at 2 p.m. is anomalous while 91% during the nightly ETL window is normal — which a static 85% threshold misses.
options: Rules use less CPU
A learned model understands contextual baselines, e.g., 72% CPU at 2 p.m. is anomalous while 91% during ETL is normal
Rules are harder to configure
Models never produce false positives
questions.q: What is the key advantage of learned anomaly detection over a rule like 'alert when CPU exceeds 85%'?

questions.explain: The chapter's pattern: 7-day rolling baseline, one-hour exclusion from baseline to prevent recent anomalies from corrupting it, and a Z-score above 3 as the alert signal.
options: 24-hour baseline, alert above 1 standard deviation
30-day baseline including the current hour
7-day rolling baseline excluding the most recent hour, alerting when the Z-score exceeds 3
No baseline — alert on any value above the mean
questions.q: How does the chapter's statistical process control query detect anomalous query execution time?

questions.explain: The missing-index DMVs reflect the indexes the optimizer wished existed during actual production execution, not a synthetic workload like DTA analyzes.
options: sys.dm_db_missing_index_details reflects real production queries, not a synthetic workload
The missing-index DMVs are faster to query
DTA was removed from SQL Server
DTA only works on Azure
questions.q: Why are the missing-index DMVs the better day-to-day index advisor than the Database Engine Tuning Advisor?

questions.explain: Graduated escalation: log the anomaly, notify if it persists, execute a pre-approved remediation script at higher severity, then escalate to on-call.
options: Kill blocking sessions immediately
Log, notify, execute a pre-approved remediation script, then escalate to on-call
Page the DBA for every anomaly
Restart the SQL Server service
questions.q: What is the graduated escalation pattern that makes automated remediation safe?

questions.explain: Every AI-generated rewrite must be tested against a production data sample for result correctness, not just performance, since subtle semantic differences can creep in.
options: Deploy it immediately — AI output is always correct
Test it against a production data sample for both correctness and performance
Only check that it runs faster
Only apply rewrites on weekends
questions.q: What must you do before deploying an AI-generated query rewrite to production?
